fig02_dataset: Corpus composition by source and label (a) and email length distribution (b).
fig01_pipeline: Experimental design: every attack has a matched control, and one backbone is read out three ways at two scales.
fig03_roc_det: Clean-test ROC (a; markers = validation-fixed operating point at FPR 0.01) and DET curves (b), where lower-left is better and differences among strong detectors are visible.
fig04_calibration: Reliability on clean test data with equal-count bins (each point averages the same number of emails); ECE uses the same bins.
fig05_vulnerability_matrix: Detection rate per detector and input manipulation at a validation-fixed FPR (a) and paired change versus the same clean emails (b). Italic columns are controls; stars mark Holm-corrected McNemar significance.
fig06_readout: Same backbone, different read-outs. (a) Detection of the same malicious emails clean, with a neutral suffix (control) and with an injected instruction. (b) Effect of the instruction itself, net of the appended text (95% CI; Holm-corrected McNemar). Filled markers: 1.5B; hollow: 3B.
fig07_padding_control: Padding with word salad (good-word attack) versus natural legitimate text of similar length. A detector whose detection rises under word salad but not under natural text is reacting to the padding artifact, not resisting padding.
fig08_asr_heatmap: Conditional attack success rate (%): share of emails detected in clean form that are missed after the manipulation. Log color scale; 0 = no successes; n/a = never detected clean.
fig09_score_plane: Per-email scores of LR-word and LoRA-1.5B on a common false-positive scale. Good-word padding moves emails left only (the lexical model misses them); natural padding moves them left and down, so both detectors miss many of the same emails.
fig10_complementarity: Error overlap between LR-word and LoRA-1.5B. Yule's Q near zero or negative means complementary errors; discordant counts are emails only one detector misses.
fig11_hybrids: Hybrid defenses versus the best single detectors (a; miss rate on a log scale; stars: Hybrid-OR vs Hybrid-Stack, Holm-corrected McNemar) and disagreement-gated triage (b; last row = review burden on legitimate mail).
fig12_adaptive: Adaptive black-box attacker: probability of evading each defense within k queries (exact over random query orders) on a log scale, with 95% bootstrap CIs at k = 1, 5, N/2 and N.
fig13_loso: Leave-one-source-out generalization of the trained detectors at a validation-fixed FPR (thresholds from the other sources): balanced accuracy, or detection rate (TPR) for sources that contain only malicious mail. n/r: not run.
fig14_heldout_source_attacks: Held-out source (Enron, 309 malicious emails): every detector was trained without Enron; thresholds from the other sources. Row labels give the realized FPR on Enron legitimate test mail.
fig15_seed_stability: LoRA-1.5B across 3 seeds (each seed redraws the training sample, initialization and order): miss rate per manipulation (a) and ASR range (b).
fig16_cost_robustness: Robustness (a: clean, mean and worst-case detection over adversarial manipulations; controls excluded) versus inference cost (b). Classical latency on CPU, SLM latency on one GPU; hybrids sum their components.
fig17_probe_layers: Linear probe by layer depth: validation AUC and detection under each manipulation (a) and the instruction effect net of the neutral suffix with 95% CI (b). Layers are selected on validation AUC only.
fig18_injection_families: Detection by template family for the neutral control and for generic and label-aware injections (unseen T_test wording). Hatched bars: 3B backbone.
fig19_attack_quality: Paraphrase attack quality after filtering: rewrites change wording (lexical similarity) while keeping meaning (semantic similarity).
fig20_lora_training: Training loss of every LoRA run (dotted: retrained without a held-out source).
fig21_threshold_free: Threshold-free instruction effect: loss of ROC-AUC caused by the instruction itself, paired over the same emails (95% CI). Filled: generic wording; hollow: label-aware wording.
fig22_natural_padding: Natural padding: detection by the share of appended benign text (a) and recovery by defenses, including LoRA trained with defender-side padding on both classes (b).
fig23_collateral_fpr: False-positive rate on the same legitimate test emails, clean and with appended text (95% CI; stars: Holm-corrected McNemar vs clean; zero plotted at 0.1%). Dotted line: target FPR 0.01.
fig24_ood_padding: Padding the attacker controls beyond the training distribution: detection rate by padding variant (a) and padding-aware LoRA across seeds versus plain LoRA and mixed-padding LoRA (b).
fig25_prompted_baselines: Stronger prompted baselines (4-shot prompt, 7B model) against the zero-shot read-outs and LoRA: clean AUC and AUC under label-aware injection (a), and the instruction effect on the AUC scale with 95% CI (b).
fig26_modern: Out-of-time test on PhishFuzzer (decontaminated against the training corpus) with thresholds fixed on the original validation split: ROC-AUC with 95% CI (a), detection rate (b) and false-positive rate (c).
fig27_readout_ablation: Read-out ablation on the primary backbone: prompted (ZS, spotlighting, 4-shot, 7B), LoRA trained to generate the label word (LoRA-Gen), probe, LoRA head on the prompted input (LoRA-Prompt) and on the raw email (LoRA), mean pooling, windowed scoring and a fine-tuned encoder. (a) AUC lost to the instruction; (b) detection under natural padding (95% CI).
fig28_score_guided_attacks: Adaptive attacks on emails each detector catches in clean form: (a) black-box padding attack success by query budget, solid: score-guided, dashed: label-only feedback, including the fused detectors; (b) white-box GCG-style suffix success on token ids and after decoding to text (95% CI).
fig29_operating_point: Natural padding at two operating points (a) and on the threshold-free scale (b): a large drop at 1% FPR with a small AUC change means padding shifts scores past a fixed threshold rather than destroying the ranking.
fig30_phish_vs_spam: Key results split by source type: phishing and fraud (Nazario, Nigerian-Fraud) vs spam-heavy sources (95% CI).
fig31_mechanism: Mechanism of the padding failure: (a) detection of naturally padded emails that fit the token budget vs those truncated; (b) pooling, input format, windowed scoring, generative training and a fine-tuned encoder under every padding variant.
fig32_realinstr_collateral: False positives on legitimate mail that carries ordinary instructions (forwarded assistant answers, IT notices, task lists) compared with the same mail clean and with an injection template (95% CI; stars: Holm-corrected McNemar vs clean).
fig33_injection_adaptive: Adaptive injection attack: score-guided search over instruction sentences addressed to the classifier vs length-matched benign sentences under the same budget. (a) success by queries; (b) paired difference on the same caught emails (95% CI).
fig34_readout_seeds: Read-out variants over seeds: each open marker is one seed, the bar is the mean. (a) natural padding; (b) worst of six padding variants.
fig35_adaptive_attacks: Adaptive attacks on emails each detector catches in clean form. (a) Score-guided and (b) label-only padding attack success by query budget (LoRA-Gen and RoBERTa-FT reach 100% like LoRA and are omitted from (a)); (c) white-box GCG suffix success after decoding to text (95% CI).
